title: Assignment 5
instructions:
Assignment – Aggregation and Business Reporting (Northwind)
Objective
Apply aggregation functions, grouping, calculated fields, and subqueries to analyze business data.

Instructions
Using the Northwind database, write SQL queries to answer the following questions.

For each question:
Write the SQL query
Run the query in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
Take a screenshot of the entire SSMS window (including query and results)
Paste both your query and the screenshot into a Word document

Questions
Find the total number of orders in the database.
Calculate the average unit price of all products.
Find the minimum and maximum product prices.
Calculate the total quantity ordered from the Order Details table.
Find the total sales amount (UnitPrice × Quantity) for all orders.
Show the total sales amount for each product (grouped by ProductID).
Show the number of orders placed by each customer.
Find customers who have placed more than 5 orders (use HAVING).
Show products whose price is greater than the average product price (use a subquery).
Calculate the total inventory value for each product (UnitPrice × UnitsInStock), and display the product name with the calculated value.
Submission Requirements
Submit one Word document
Include:
All SQL queries
Screenshots of results (full SSMS window)

File name format:
Assignment5_YourName

Notes
Use appropriate aggregation functions (SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX)
Use GROUP BY where required
Use HAVING for filtering grouped data
Use subqueries where specified
Use calculated fields for derived values

questions.prompt: Find the total number of orders in the database.
questions.answer:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS TotalOrders
FROM Orders;

questions.prompt: Calculate the average unit price of all products.
questions.answer:
SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) AS AvgPrice
FROM Products;

questions.prompt: Find the minimum and maximum product prices.
Calculate the total quantity ordered from the Order Details table.
questions.answer:
SELECT SUM(Quantity) AS TotalQuantity
FROM [Order Details];

questions.prompt: Find the total sales amount (UnitPrice × Quantity) for all orders.
questions.answer:
SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) AS TotalSales
FROM [Order Details];

questions.prompt: Show the total sales amount for each product (grouped by ProductID).
questions.answer:
SELECT ProductID,
       SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) AS TotalSales
FROM [Order Details]
GROUP BY ProductID;

questions.prompt: Show the number of orders placed by each customer.
questions.answer:
SELECT CustomerID,
       COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID;

questions.prompt: Find customers who have placed more than 5 orders (use HAVING).
questions.answer:
SELECT CustomerID,
       COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

questions.prompt: Show products whose price is greater than the average product price (use a subquery).
Calculate the total inventory value for each product (UnitPrice × UnitsInStock), and display the product name with the calculated value.

title: Assignment 7
instructions:
Assignment – JOINs and Business Reporting (Northwind)
Objective
Use JOINs to combine data from multiple tables and answer business questions using SQL.

Instructions
Using the Northwind database, write SQL queries to answer the following questions.

For each question:
Write the SQL query
Run the query in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
Take a screenshot of the entire SSMS window (query + results)
Paste both your query and screenshot into a Word document
You may use the Query Designer tool in SSMS to help build your queries, but you must include the final SQL query in your submission.

Questions
Display the CompanyName of customers and their OrderDate by joining Customers and Orders. 
Display CompanyName and Freight for orders where Freight is greater than 50. 
Display CompanyName and OrderDate using a JOIN between Customers and Orders. 
Display CompanyName, OrderDate, and ProductName by joining Customers, Orders, Order Details, and Products. 
Display ProductName and Quantity ordered for each order. 
Display ProductName and the total inventory value (UnitPrice × UnitsInStock) for each product. 
Show the total amount spent by each customer (CompanyName). 
Find the total quantity sold for each product where the total quantity is greater than 100. 
Display CompanyName and OrderDate for orders placed after January 1, 1997. 
Which 10 products generate the highest revenue? 
Submission Requirements
Submit one Word document
Include:
All SQL queries
Screenshots (full SSMS window)

File name format:
Assignment7_YourName

Notes
Use:
INNER JOIN
Table aliases
GROUP BY
SUM
Use calculated fields where needed
There may be multiple correct solutions

questions.prompt: Display the CompanyName of customers and their OrderDate by joining Customers and Orders.
Display CompanyName and Freight for orders where Freight is greater than 50.
questions.answer:
SELECT c.CompanyName, o.Freight
FROM Customers c
INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.Freight > 50;

questions.prompt: Display CompanyName and OrderDate using a JOIN between Customers and Orders.
Display CompanyName, OrderDate, and ProductName by joining Customers, Orders, Order Details, and Products.
questions.answer:
SELECT c.CompanyName, o.OrderDate, p.ProductName
FROM Customers c
INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
INNER JOIN [Order Details] od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
INNER JOIN Products p ON od.ProductID = p.ProductID;

questions.prompt: Display ProductName and Quantity ordered for each order.
Display ProductName and the total inventory value (UnitPrice × UnitsInStock) for each product.
questions.answer:
SELECT ProductName, UnitPrice * UnitsInStock AS InventoryValue
FROM Products;

questions.prompt: Show the total amount spent by each customer (CompanyName).
questions.answer:
SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity) AS TotalSpent
FROM Customers c
INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
INNER JOIN [Order Details] od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
GROUP BY c.CompanyName;

questions.prompt: Find the total quantity sold for each product where the total quantity is greater than 100.
questions.answer:
SELECT p.ProductName, SUM(od.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity
FROM Products p
INNER JOIN [Order Details] od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
GROUP BY p.ProductName
HAVING SUM(od.Quantity) > 100;

questions.prompt: Display CompanyName and OrderDate for orders placed after January 1, 1997.
questions.answer:
SELECT c.CompanyName, o.OrderDate
FROM Customers c
INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.OrderDate > '1997-01-01';

questions.prompt: Which 10 products generate the highest revenue?
questions.answer:
SELECT TOP 10 p.ProductName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity) AS Revenue
FROM Products p
INNER JOIN [Order Details] od ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
GROUP BY p.ProductName
ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

title: Assignment 9
instructions:
Assignment 9 – SQL Functions
Objective
Use built-in SQL functions to transform, analyze, and present data for business purposes.
Instructions
Using the Northwind database, write SQL queries to answer the following questions.
For each question:
Write the SQL query that creates a stored procedure
Run the query in SQL and execute the stored procedure
Take a screenshot of the entire SSMS window (execution + results)
Paste both your query and screenshot into a Word document

Questions
Display CompanyName, its uppercase version, and the number of characters in the name. 
Display OrderID, OrderDate, and Order Year. Only include orders placed in 1997. 
Display ProductName, UnitPrice, and a rounded price (no decimals). Only include products with UnitPrice greater than 20. 
Display CustomerID, CompanyName, and Region. Replace NULL values in Region with 'Unknown'. Only include customers from USA. 
Display ProductName and UnitPrice. Also show a new column that calculates price after a 10% increase. Sort the results based on the increased price from highest to lowest.
Submission Requirements
Submit one Word document
Include:
All SQL queries
Screenshots (full SSMS window)
File name format:
Assignment9_YourName
Notes
Use: 
Text functions (UPPER, LEN, etc.) 
Date functions (YEAR, GETDATE if needed) 
Math functions (ROUND) 
NULL handling (IS NULL, ISNULL) 
You may combine multiple functions in one query 
Ensure your queries run without errors 
There may be multiple correct solutions
There may be multiple correct solutions
note: General instructions mention stored procedures, but the questions and supplied key use SELECT queries. Review follows the questions and key.

questions.prompt: Display CompanyName, its uppercase version, and the number of characters in the name.
questions.answer:
SELECT 
    CompanyName,
    UPPER(CompanyName) AS CompanyName_Upper,
    LEN(CompanyName) AS NameLength
FROM Customers;

questions.prompt: Display OrderID, OrderDate, and Order Year. Only include orders placed in 1997.
questions.answer:
SELECT 
    OrderID,
    OrderDate,
    YEAR(OrderDate) AS OrderYear
FROM Orders
WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 1997;

questions.prompt: Display ProductName, UnitPrice, and a rounded price (no decimals). Only include products with UnitPrice greater than 20.
questions.answer:
-- Only include products with UnitPrice > 20
SELECT 
    ProductName,
    UnitPrice,
    ROUND(UnitPrice, 0) AS RoundedPrice
FROM Products
WHERE UnitPrice > 20;

questions.prompt: Display CustomerID, CompanyName, and Region. Replace NULL values in Region with 'Unknown'. Only include customers from USA.
questions.answer:
-- Replace NULL Region values with 'Unknown'
-- Only include customers from USA
SELECT 
    CustomerID,
    CompanyName,
    ISNULL(Region, 'Unknown') AS Region
FROM Customers
WHERE Country = 'USA';

questions.prompt: Display ProductName and UnitPrice. Also show a new column that calculates price after a 10% increase. Sort the results based on the increased price from highest to lowest.
questions.answer:
-- Sort by increased price from highest to lowest
SELECT 
    ProductName,
    UnitPrice,
    UnitPrice * 1.10 AS IncreasedPrice
FROM Products
ORDER BY IncreasedPrice DESC;
